Extension Architecture Guide

This short introduction summarizes the architecture guide and links to the detailed sections below.

Design the extraction stage

The extraction stage receives the rendered document and identifies the meaningful page content. It must preserve headings, paragraphs, lists, links, images, tables, and code while excluding navigation, account controls, advertising, cookie prompts, and unrelated recommendations. A quality check compares candidate lengths so a short summary is not mistaken for the complete technical document.

Documentation sites often place an introductory article beside a series of sibling sections inside the main element. Selecting only the introductory article would technically return content but would omit most of the page. The semantic fallback therefore remains important even when Readability returns a non-empty result.

Convert the complete document

After extraction, the converter produces deterministic GitHub Flavored Markdown. Links use absolute URLs, code blocks retain their language, tables remain structured, and the page title appears exactly once. The conversion runs locally and does not send the source document to any external service.

Browser-level tests invoke the real extension action, wait for the popup, inspect generated Markdown, retry the conversion, and verify protected-page errors. This final section must be present in the exported output or the quality comparison has selected an incomplete candidate.
